newsitem.title: USA: Imation sees Q2 EPS below analysts view.
newsitem.headline: Imation sees Q2 EPS below analysts view.

text.p: Imation Corp, an imaging and information company, said on Tuesday it expects second quarter earnings to fall below analysts estimates which it said ranged between $0.30 and $0.38 a share based on preliminary financial data through May.
The company reported an operating profit, before special charges, of $0.11 a share in the 1996 second quarter.
Imation also said operating margins for the quarter will likely be in the low single digits.

The company cited weaker than expected demand for several lower- capacity data storage products -- including the low end Travan mini-cartridges resulting in lower gross margins than previously planned.

Imation also said that its broader portfolio of imaging and information products serving the medical imaging, printing and publishing, photo color and data center markets continues to meet its current expectations, based on preliminary financial data through May.
"The information technology industry is experiencing increased demand for higher-capacity desktop and networked storage solutions," said Bill Monahan, Imation chief executive, in a news release.
He said the company will be addressing this demand in late 1997 and 1998 with an expanded product portfolio.
Imation said it is scheduled to announce second quarter earnings on July 30, 1997.
Imation shares were up 1/16 at 25-7/16 Tuesday.
